newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless rise worse than expected - analysts.
newsitem.headline: German jobless rise worse than expected - analysts.

text.p: A huge rise in January German unadjusted unemployment to a post-war record of over 4.6 million, although worse than expected, did not provoke analysts to revise up their forecasts for adjusted data.
The unadjusted rise, published in newspapers and confirmed by the opposition Social Democrats, "was clearly worse than expected", said Luther Hessler of Trinkaus Capital Management.
But analysts contacted by Reuters said they were not upping their estimates for a rise in the underlying, seasonally adjusted jobless rate. The data is due this morning.

Gernot Nerb at Salomon Brothers in Frankfurt said he expected a rise of 40,000 in the adjusted figure from December's 4.16. That is below a Reuters consensus forecast of a rise of 52,000, based on a survey of economists.
Hessler said that the increase would boost chance of a cut in interest rates by the Bundesbank to stimulate a German economy whose recovery is become increasingly uncertain.
